title: FrontendSurfaceManifest
description: The single machine-readable manifest of the public source-first authoring surface. Public-export scans, documentation-alignment checks, and generated reference docs derive from this one manifest. Every declaration must carry a projection for every registered language, and the projection is checked by argument shape rather than by name: a language with no projection for a declaration is not a conforming implementation of the surface. This manifest carries no AIR/AIS operation string and no lowering identity.

everyday.description: Everyday source declarations for model-backed Agents and general Workflows.

advanced.description: The advanced names imported only when their behavior is needed. `capability` declares a handler a package ships, as against `Capability`, which references one. `Skill` declares instructions a program can load; it is not a second way to declare a persona, it is the one way, and like every other declaration it is stated at module scope and named by the body that loads it — no declaration is listed again on the Agent. `source` is the one name a TypeScript module states about itself, because JavaScript cannot read its own text back; Python infers the same fact.

non_public.description: Names that are contract/lowering identities and MUST NOT be exported by installable authoring packages nor taught as author API.

languages.description: Every language that implements the surface. Registration is what makes conformance mechanical: a declaration missing a projection for a registered language is FrontendSurfaceIncomplete. Adding a language means adding an entry here and one language-local extraction layer in the conformance gate; every declaration, argument, and diagnostic is inherited.

vocabularies.description: Every generated closed vocabulary the surface publishes on its own author-facing import path, and where each language publishes it. A vocabulary is not a declaration: it carries no arguments and produces no intent, it is the set of values a declaration's arguments are written with. Each is stated here so the import path an author is taught is a fact the manifest owns rather than one each document remembers, and so `exported_from_root: false` — the invariant that a vocabulary stays off the root namespace the tiers pin exactly — is declared rather than merely observed.

types.description: Shared executable type contracts. These are not authoring factories and produce no second source intent.

declarations.description: Every public declaration/marker: its per-language projections, the bound semantic node, its accepted arguments and how each language projects them, its produced intent, and the diagnostics it can raise.

authoring_root.description: Repository-relative module whose public exports are exactly the declarations this language marks `exported_from_root`.

generated_diagnostics.description: Repository-relative generated module projecting `declarations[].diagnostics`. Drift against this manifest is FrontendSurfaceUnsynced.

VocabularyProjection.description: How one language publishes one vocabulary: the repository-relative module that re-exports the generated names, the import path an author writes, and whether the authoring root re-exports it — which is always false, because the root publishes exactly the tiered declaration names.

SurfaceVocabulary.description: One generated closed vocabulary and its per-language public import path. A registered language absent here is FrontendSurfaceIncomplete, exactly as it is for a declaration.

generated_by.description: The codegen arm that mints the names, so the vocabulary has one source and this manifest states where it surfaces rather than what it contains.

SurfaceProjection.description: How one language projects one declaration: the module that defines it, the exported symbol, the optional member the arguments are taken from, whether the authoring root exports it, and the author-facing signature. A language that derives a declaration instead of asking the author for it says so with `inferred`, which is how an asymmetric obligation — one language states it, the other works it out — stays visible to the gate rather than being absent from the manifest.

inferred.description: This language derives the declaration rather than publishing an author-facing name for it. `symbol` then names the definition that does the deriving, the gate proves that definition exists and is not exported from the authoring root, and every argument must be projected `inferred` here.

ProjectedAs.description: The closed set of forms an argument can take in a language. `inferred` means the language derives the argument rather than accepting it, and the gate proves the projection does not accept it as a parameter.

projections.description: One projection per registered language. A registered language absent here is FrontendSurfaceIncomplete.

produces_intent.description: The FrontendGraph call_intent or control_intent kind produced when this declaration is invoked in a body, if any.

diagnostics.description: Closed diagnostic codes this marker/declaration can raise, anchored to the offending marker/argument/callsite.
